question: For white-on-red signs, what minimum maintained retroreflectivity values and contrast criterion are shown in Table 2A-5?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For white-on-red signs (e.g., STOP signs), Table 2A-5 specifies a minimum maintained retroreflectivity of W ≥ 35 and R ≥ 7 (in cd/lx/m², measured at an observation angle of 0.2° and an entrance angle of −4.0°), and this single set of values applies across all sheeting types listed. In addition, footnote 4 imposes a minimum sign contrast ratio of ≥ 3:1, computed as white retroreflectivity divided by red retroreflectivity. Agencies must use an assessment or management method designed to keep signs at or above these levels. Standards (mandatory): - "Public agencies or officials having jurisdiction shall use an assessment or management method that is designed to maintain sign retroreflectivity at or above the minimum levels in Table 2A-5." - "Regulatory, warning, and guide signs (see Section 2A.03), and object markers, shall be retroreflective or illuminated to show the same shape and similar color by both day and night, unless otherwise provided in this Manual for a particular sign or group of signs." - "Regulatory signs shall be retroreflective or illuminated (see Section 2A.21)." Guidance (recommended): - Except for signs specifically identified in Paragraph 5 of Section 2A.22, one or more of the methods described in "Maintaining Traffic Sign Retroreflectivity" (FHWA-SA-07-020, Revised 2013), or a method developed based on an engineering study, should be used to maintain sign retroreflectivity at or above the minimum levels in Table 2A-5; signs identified as below the minimum levels should be replaced. Visual evidence: [Image 3] shows Table 2A-5, in which the "White on Red" row reads "W ≥ 35; R ≥ 7" spanning all sheeting-type columns, with the "Additional Criteria" column referencing footnote 4, which states "Minimum sign contrast ratio ≥ 3:1 (white retroreflectivity ÷ red retroreflectivity)"; the table's footnote 1 states the values are in cd/lx/m² measured at an observation angle of 0.2° and an entrance angle of −4.0°. [Image 1] provides the surrounding Section 2A.22 text (Support, Guidance, and Option paragraphs) tied to Table 2A-5. [Image 2] shows page 62 with the Section 2A.22 Standard requiring agencies to maintain retroreflectivity at or above the Table 2A-5 minimums. Citations: - Table 2A-5 (p.62) - Section 2A.22 Standard §2 (p.62) - Section 2A.22 Guidance §4 (p.62) - Section 2A.21 Standard §3 (p.62) - Section 2B.01 Standard §3 (p.67) - Page 104
gold_answer: White at least 35 cd/lx/m², red at least 7 cd/lx/m², and a white-to-red contrast ratio of at least 3:1.
